unique_findings: SKU-level "AI visibility" / conversational ranking metric — they claim per-SKU intelligence that measures how a product ranks inside LLM responses. That implies they are instrumenting prompts, parsing model outputs, mapping free-text LLM answers back to structured SKUs, and scoring conversational relevance instead of classic keyword search relevance.

Bidirectional PIM/ERP sync focused on agentic metadata — they emphasize two-way syncing, suggesting not just pushing product data to the platform but ingesting agent-driven signals (prompts, visibility scores, conversion events) back into merchants' PIM/ERP to close the loop. This requires schema-mapping, conflict resolution, and near-real-time reconciliation across heterogeneous enterprise systems.

Prompt-level demand research as signal source — collecting and aggregating user prompts (and likely resulting assistant responses) to derive trends and demand volume per SKU. That's a different telemetry stream than pageviews or clicks: it treats prompts as first-class demand telemetry and requires normalization, intent clustering, and volume estimation from sparse, noisy prompt text.

Automated content optimization targeted at LLM consumption — instead of classic SEO, they optimize product metadata/content to improve conversational ranking inside AI agents. This implies generation/transformation of structured metadata (attributes, long/short descriptions, semantic tags, embeddings) specifically tuned to how LLMs surface and cite products.

Multi-platform AI discovery integration layer — they list integrations with ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Google AI Mode, Perplexity and claim pilot support for Agentic Commerce Protocol / Instant Checkout. Supporting multiple closed/proprietary LLM ecosystems in parallel requires an abstraction layer that normalizes different plugin/agent APIs, differing response formats, and variable support for programmatic checkout.

Instrumenting "purchasable inside agents" — making a catalog not only discoverable but transactible inside assistants implies implementing agent checkout hooks, payment tokenization, consent/authorization UX flows for agents, and fraud/authorization controls that work across assistant platforms.

Data infrastructure for cross-model measurement — to report AI visibility they must continuously query or simulate many agents, store model outputs, and run matching/attribution pipelines to attribute LLM suggestions to SKUs. That is non-trivial operational work and requires robust offline and streaming pipelines plus deduping and confidence scoring.
